Visual Indicators of Smart Glasses

As wearable technology gains popularity, concerns regarding covert surveillance have increased. While some smart glasses are designed to look like standard eyewear, many feature thicker frames at the temples to house internal hardware, such as camera lenses, ports, or indicator LEDs that activate during recording.

Behavioral Clues and Digital Detection

Beyond physical appearance, observers might notice individuals pressing temple buttons, whispering voice commands, or appearing distracted by heads-up displays. Additionally, mobile applications such as 'Nearby Glasses' and 'ZuckOff' attempt to scan for Bluetooth signals associated with these devices. However, these tools are not foolproof; Bluetooth can be disabled, and false positives are common. For detailed guidance on identifying these devices and managing privacy concerns, visit the official report at https://www.engadget.com/2296049/best-ways-tell-if-someone-wearing-ai-glasses/
